articles.title: What community means for a wine shop along Maginhawa Street
articles.summary: Through the Maginhawa Food Community, Rose Abes has found support among fellow entrepreneurs navigating the fulfillment and challenges of running their own establishments

items: Rose Abes, owner of La Rosa Vino, emphasizes the importance of community and collaboration with neighboring businesses in Quezon City, as seen in her Wine and Food Hop event.
Since opening in February 2023, Rose has successfully built a customer base and created a welcoming space for wine lovers, particularly women, while navigating a male-dominated industry.

The Maginhawa Food Community (MFC) plays a crucial role in supporting local businesses, allowing Rose to collaborate with other establishments and promote a shared goal of sustaining small businesses in the area.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – For a business owner, sending customers out the door would normally be the opposite of the goal. But for Rose Abes, owner of La Rosa Vino, sharing customers with her neighbors is part of how she does business.

On September 19, La Rosa Vino once again brought guests to walk along Maginhawa Street, Quezon City for its fourth Wine and Food Hop. This year, its day-long event paired wines with signature dishes from six partner restaurants in the neighborhood.
For Rose, these partnerships are built on something simple.
“A good relationship is very important,” she said, referring to her connection with the Maginhawa Food Community (MFC) and fellow business owners.

This is a philosophy that has shaped La Rosa Vino since Rose opened the business in February 2023. What began as her passion for wine came with a goal: to build a community of wine drinkers in Quezon City, where she saw fewer spaces devoted to wine compared with areas like Makati.

blocks.caption: FOR EVERYONE. Guests of the Wine and Food Hop include previous customers and fellow business owners from the Maginhawa Food Community. Photo from La Rosa Vino

blocks.text: But building that community also meant finding her own place in an industry she acknowledges remains largely dominated by men.
“I just need to be me,” Rose said in an interview with Rappler. “Wala akong magagawa (There’s nothing I can do) since it’s really male-dominated. So, I just need to be myself.”
Ever since she opened her wine shop, Rose has continuously grown her customer base and has found consistent support from the MFC.

Before Rose found herself as a wine shop owner, she was working in marketing and events. When the pandemic prompted her to reconsider her career, she decided to turn her passion for wine into a business of her own.
Finally, her lockdown-born passion for wine led her to change careers. She decided to take her knowledge, wine and spirit certifications, and dream to create a little nook for wine lovers.
While Rose admits that La Rosa Vino is still young, she is also proud to share that she has seen a good increase in wine lovers who now frequent her shop.
Beyond selling bottles of wine, Rose has continued introducing activities that encourage customers to explore alcoholic beverages in different ways.
“My goal of bringing my customers an experience remains,” she said.
In 2025, Rose hosted various activities in her shop partnered with the experience of drinking wine, such as vegan dining, yoga sessions, floral arrangements, and more.
This year, Rose leaned more into experiencing the alcoholic beverages themselves — one of which was a whiskey appreciation class.

“A lot of my customers showed interest in appreciation classes. It’s a deeper experience compared to what we hosted before, so I thought maybe it would not be a hit. Surprisingly, we were fully booked within two weeks!” she shared.

blocks.caption: WOMAN-OWNED. Rose Abes (center) joins fellow participants during the Wine and Food Hop. Photo from La Rosa Vino

blocks.text: Rose has also noticed that many of La Rosa Vino’s customers and event participants are women, something she believes may reflect their desire for spaces where they can enjoy and feel safe at the same time.
“I’m happy that La Rosa Vino is a comfortable space for them to enjoy alcoholic drinks. Like me, maybe they are also looking for a place to be themselves freely,” she explained.
“Perhaps the shop being woman-owned adds to that comfort,” she said.
But the intimate community Rose has built extends beyond the customers who visit La Rosa Vino.
Through the MFC, she has also found support among fellow entrepreneurs navigating the fulfillment and challenges of running their own establishments.
While her background in marketing helped her establish La Rosa Vino, Rose admitted that managing a physical business came with its own challenges.
Being part of the MFC, however gave her opportunities to collaborate with neighboring restaurants, including through La Rosa Vino’s annual Wine and Food Hop.
Formed in 2021, this network of business owners has grown from a small group of restaurant owners into a collective of 70 members.

According to its president, Jules Guiang, they started with around five restaurants and initially struggled to establish credibility among restaurant owners. They gradually earned their trust through initiatives involving local government coordination and events such as the Maginhawa Arts and Food Festival.

“We advocate for Maginhawa to remain a hub for micro and small businesses, many of which are family-owned,” said Guiang. “The MFC works to bring these concerns to the local government, especially as the area attracts more customers.”
He said the group wants to help smaller establishments remain in business and potentially grow, rather than be crowded out by larger brands.

blocks.caption: LONG-RUNNING. Wadough owner Wado Siman shares his café’s success. Photo from La Rosa Vino

blocks.text: One of the MFC’s members is Wadough’s, a pastry shop known for its minimalist cakes, including the viral wedding cake it made for actress Bea Alonzo. The shop was also the third stop on La Rosa Vino’s Wine and Food Hop.

“When I opened this café nine years ago, I imagined it as a place where I would sit down with customers and chat with them while having coffee and cake. The goal was that,” said owner Wado Siman, recalling that they never really expected the shop to be famous.

Wado believes that most of his shop’s fame is brought by pure luck, especially with the timing of going viral online during the pandemic. This success led him to gain more customers, which naturally brought customers to nearby restaurants too.

For Rose, the Wine and Food Hop is one way to put that shared goal into practice. By bringing her customers to neighboring establishments, La Rosa Vino helps introduce them to other independent businesses along Maginhawa while giving participating restaurants another opportunity to reach customers.

The event also reflects how Rose approaches running her own business. Rather than focusing solely on bringing people into La Rosa Vino, she sees value in encouraging them to explore the neighborhood and discover what other establishments have to offer.
“The MFC is very supportive with its business owners, both emotionally and physically,” Rose said, recalling that the collective helped her during her first year running a physical establishment.

blocks.caption: COMMUNITY. Guests gather around to toast the start of the Wine and Food Hop event. Photo by Elle Guison/Rappler

blocks.text: Over time, her fellow business owners have also become her friends. When asked how she found her partner establishments, she replied that they were very casual invitations of “isasali kita sa next Wine and Food Hop ko, ha? (I’ll include you in my next Wine and Food Hop, okay?)”
For Rose, these relationships have become part of how La Rosa Vino operates.
She has always envisioned La Rosa Vino developing a community that includes not only the customers who visit her shop, but also the independent businesses that share Maginhawa Street.
After all, she believes that wine is better enjoyed with company. – Rappler.com

articles.summary: India says Chinese forces deviating from established patrolling patterns continue to disrupt the border situation, a day after the ITBP chief reported face-offs at multiple locations in Arunachal…

India blames Chinese patrolling deviations for border disruptions

blocks.caption: India's China border police chief has said that face-offs between Indian and Chinese troops are continuing at multiple locations in Arunachal Pradesh [FILE: November 29, 2022]Image: Manish Swarup/AP/picture alliance

blocks.text: India's Foreign Ministry said on Friday the situation along the India-China border was periodically disrupted when Chinese forces deviated from established patrolling patterns.

"Both sides continue to use existing diplomatic and military mechanisms to resolve outstanding issues and avoid misunderstandings and miscalculations along the Line of Actual Control (LAC)," the ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said while addressing the media.
The two countries have also agreed to discuss ways to improve their understanding of the LAC in certain areas to strengthen border management, he added.
"I would also like to emphasize that maintaining peace and tranquillity in the border areas is essential for the overall development of bilateral relations," Jaiswal said.
'Face-offs between Indian and Chinese troops continuing'

This development comes a day after India's China border police chief, Shatrujeet Singh Kapur, said on Thursday that face-offs between Indian and Chinese troops are continuing at multiple locations along the border in the northeastern state of Arunachal Pradesh, despite ongoing talks between the two countries, according to Indian media.
The face-offs in Arunachal Pradesh underscore the challenges of maintaining peace along the border even as the two countries have held several rounds of military and diplomatic talks this year.

The issue was also taken up by the opposition Congress party with Member of Parliament and senior party leader Jairam Ramesh criticizing Prime Minister Narendra Modi and and the government for "remain silent on this grave issue."
"The nation is asking: Amid ongoing tensions on the border, what kind of nationalism is this softness toward China and the growing economic dependence?" Ramesh posted on X.

"De Lima, as a lawyer and former human rights advocate, you know that every person has the right to protect themselves from any accusation. Filing a case through the legal process is not an attack on the freedom of speech, but a right that every citizen has," Duterte said in Bisaya.

On Friday, Duterte lodged a libel and cyber libel complaint against National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Melvin Matibag and dismissed policeman Rodulfo Gracioso Jr. over claims of cash delivery to their family.
Executives and journalists of GMA Network were also included in the complaint.
Hours after the filing, De Lima issued a statement saying the complaint was meant to strike fear among media practitioners.

"This is clearly an attempt to silence journalists and truth-seekers, depriving them of their freedom of the press. Filing a libel case against a media network and its journalists for doing their job of reporting allegations of corruption sends a chilling message to other media practitioners," said De Lima, who also serves as senior deputy minority leader of the House of Representatives.
However, Duterte insisted that press freedom has its limits when it violates the rights of others.

"Freedom of the press is important for democracy, but it comes with the responsibility to ensure the safety of those who report and give opportunities to the other side to respond. Reporting an allegation and proving it to be true are two different things," Duterte said.
Reminding De Lima she previously faced controversies and allegations, Duterte said he hopes that her stance on justice and the right to defense remains unchanged.

De Lima was a justice secretary and senator who was a staunch critic of the Davao City congressman's father, former president Rodrigo Duterte. She was jailed in February 2017 during the Duterte administration and spent nearly seven years in detention on drug-related charges. All of her charges were cleared in June 2024.

"A person's right should not be defended at the expense of their own safety, which can be used as a pretext to silence the media. In the same way, freedom of speech should not be used to silence others who are asking for justice," Paolo Duterte said, as he called for a fair, evidence-based process to dispute allegations instead of what he called prejudiced judgment.
As a parting shot to De Lima, Duterte said, "Just stay in Congress, be cute, smile, smile."
In a statement, GMA Network said it has yet to receive a copy of the complaint.
"We will review the matter and comment accordingly upon receipt," it said.

Gracioso previously alleged that he delivered cash to former president Duterte, congressman Duterte, and his sister Vice President Sara Duterte upon the instruction of former House speaker Lord Allan Velasco.
The Davao City lawmaker has dismissed Gracioso's claims as "pure fiction."
The vice president has also denied the allegations and filed her affidavit with the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI).
Velasco's camp has said the allegations against him have "no basis." — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: France prepares for day of protest a week after nationwide riots
articles.summary: More than 70,000 police officers are to be deployed over fears protesters will defy restrictions on demonstrations.

blocks.text: France is on high alert ahead of a new day of nationwide protests on Saturday, a week after the country saw some of its worst unrest in decades.

Sweeping restrictions have been imposed on demonstrations across France but hundreds of thousands of protesters are still expected to gather in Paris and elsewhere for a second round of protests organised by students, trade unions and wider anti-government groups.

The interior ministry has said it will deploy 70,000 police officers, ramping up the security presence in French cities, after the government was accused by opposition parties of failing to foresee the scale of the unrest on 17 October.
"We will not let anything go unchallenged," said Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez.

"We will be uncompromising with the vandals, with the looters, and all those who commit acts of violence," he added, explaining that separate from the planned protests, numerous calls for violence had been seen on social media from the "far left and radical extreme left".
Hundreds of people have been jailed for vandalism, arson and looting after fast-track court hearings in recent days.

President Emmanuel Macron met high-school students' representatives on Friday ahead of Saturday's protests, and although they said he had made clear commitments to them, they said students should "continue to mobilise".

Macron decreed earlier this week that only demonstrations organised by a recognised trade unions would be permitted to take place on Saturday, and several key cities including Lyon, Nice and Montpellier have gone further by announcing blanket bans on gatherings.
Official announcements appear to have done little to deter organisers, with hundreds of large and small demonstrations planned across France.

After a week in which some cities have lived under partial curfews - including areas of the capital - there is an inconsistent picture across France's cities as to what level of protest will be permitted by authorities.

While some mayors have pressed ahead with broad bans, others have agreed to allow demonstrations registered with authorities - for example, in Marseille, a previous order barring all protests was swiftly reversed to allow a trade union-organised march to go ahead.

In Paris, a march organised by the student trade union and supported by labour groups has been ordered to stick to a route which does not go through the city centre - though preparations for unrest in some of the city's most recognisable areas are under way regardless.

The Louvre, Orsay and Picasso museums will all be closed on Saturday, a scheduled home match for football team PSG has been moved to Monday, and some businesses have boarded up their windows in anticipation of further looting.

In a sign of how a student-led protest movement expanded to become a wider anti-government outpouring, protesters associated with a revived gilet jaunes (yellow-vest) movement could be out in force across France on Saturday.
The protest movement, which has attracted support from left and right, led huge disruptive demonstrations during Macron's first term in office.
A website associated with the group listed more than 500 planned demonstrations and some 200 other actions on Saturday, and demanded that Macron resign.
In its online call for action, the group said "we refuse to add our voices to the chorus of outrage" over the violence on 17 October and accused police of attacking protesters.

France is still reeling from last week's unrest, which saw police vastly outnumbered by protesters and rioters, shops looted and buildings torched - perhaps most emblematically, the ornate 19th-Century town hall in Limoges.

On Friday, Justice Minister Gérald Darmanin said 232 people had been imprisoned for their role in the 17 October riots, and more than 1,100 had appeared in court. Around 260 of those cases involves "charges of organised gang activity", he added.

Darmanin has ordered prosecutors to seek punitive measures against people convicted of looting or attacking police officers, including banning them from taking part in demonstrations, removing their right to vote and barring them from accessing social media.

Disillusionment is high among the French public, who have seen cost-of-living pressures increase, and who are faced with increasingly dire warnings that any future government will likely have to make deep spending cuts in order to finance spiralling levels of debt.

On top of that, the recent unrest has played out against the backdrop of a polarised political landscape and with France preparing for what could be the most divisive and unpredictable election period in a generation.
Macron will leave office next spring and polls suggest a candidate from his centrist movement could fail to make it through to a run-off vote in May between the top two contenders.
That would likely leave French voters to choose between the hard-right National Rally and radical-left La France Insoumise (France Unbowed).

Leading figures from both parties have levelled the blame for the disorder at Macron and his ministers, sensing fertile ground among the French public after a period in which his centrist party has struggled to form functioning governments and pass legislation.

Jean-Luc Mélenchon, the leader and presidential candidate of La France Insoumise, has criticised what he has framed as heavy-handed policing of demonstrations and has accused Macron of "destroying the republican state" by imposing restrictions.
He has called on his supporters to join protests on Saturday as he did the previous week, before condemning the rioting which followed.
A two-day National Rally conference in Orléans, around 120 km (75 miles) to the south of Paris, could prove to be a flashpoint on Saturday.
Left-wing groups are expected to descend on the small city, where thousands of members of the hard-right party are set to gather to hear its leader Marine Le Pen speak.

This week, the city's mayor warned the numbers expected in Orléans were "unprecedented", and said thousands of police would be deployed to manage any clashes, adding that public transport would be suspended.

Opinion polls suggest Le Pen could have her strongest chance yet of becoming president as she runs for a fourth time, despite a court finding her guilty of embezzling EU funds earlier this year. She has denied committing any offence and is appealing the verdict.

articles.title: Arrest made after fire at Hitler's Eagle's Nest retreat
articles.summary: Around 200 emergency personnel are deployed to fight the blaze at the Nazi dictator's Alpine residence in Germany.

blocks.text: Police in the south German state of Bavaria have detained a suspect during a fire at Adolf Hitler's Alpine mountain retreat, the Kehlsteinhaus, also known as the Eagle's Nest.
Dispatchers in Traunstein received a fire alarm from the building at 21:15 (19:15 GMT) on Friday, and firefighters found it engulfed in flames.
Difficult terrain was hindering efforts to extinguish the blaze and it was still burning early on Saturday, police said, with some 200 emergency personnel deployed. There were no reports of injuries.
The Nazi dictator used the retreat, which lies above the town of Berchtesgaden, as a part-time seat of government and met commanders there to plan the invasion of the USSR in 1941.
A criminal investigation is under way to determine whether the suspect is connected to the fire.
Hitler also used the area as a backdrop for propaganda films portraying him as a lover of animals and nature.

articles.title: Martha Sazon, GCash’s newly Mynted billionaire
articles.summary: Make way for the fintech queen: top dog of the PSE’s seventh-largest local company, one of Asia’s most powerful women, and now, a paper billionaire

blocks.text: Make way for the fintech queen: top dog of the PSE’s seventh-largest local company, one of Asia’s most powerful women, and now, a paper billionaire

items: Martha Sazon, CEO of Mynt, celebrated the company's IPO at the Philippine Stock Exchange, marking a significant milestone in her career and making her a billionaire.
Sazon's journey to leadership included diverse experiences in banking and marketing, culminating in her role at Mynt during the pandemic, which accelerated GCash's growth.
Looking ahead, Sazon aims to expand Mynt's lending services, allocating a significant portion of IPO proceeds to enhance this revenue stream while navigating the volatile stock market.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

Martha Sazon stood on the trading floor of the Philippine Stock Exchange, huddled with her core leadership team, and took a selfie with no less than President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. It was a busy morning for Mynt’s top boss, who had overseen GCash’s spectacular rise into a fintech unicorn and was now ringing the bell on the biggest IPO in Philippine history.
Now, her moment of reckoning.

blocks.caption: PUBLIC. Martha Sazon and Mynt’s leadership team pose for a photo with President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. at Mynt’s IPO ceremony on Tuesday, October 20. Photo from Sazon’s LinkedIn.

blocks.text: With the toll of that bell, her considerable fortune has a public price tag. At Mynt’s P6.60 IPO price, her 220.1 million shares were worth a cool P1.45 billion. Sazon was also offering about 44 million of her shares for sale, potentially pocketing P290.55 million before taxes and fees, while keeping another 176.1 million shares worth P1.16 billion.
Cheers to the newly Mynted billionaire.

Of course, this moment didn’t magically make Mynt’s president and CEO rich. Those shares were valuable even before the initial public offering (IPO), when Mynt was still privately held. But an IPO is everybody’s favorite liquidity event, and Sazon — like GCash’s early private equity backers — turned some of that paper wealth into actual cash.
Quite the reward for someone who wasn’t around when GCash started in 2004, back when it felt more like a fun party trick for Globe users to send money via SMS.

Sazon’s journey to the top of fintech took more than a few turns. A University of the Philippines (UP) accountancy graduate, she started her career in banking, where the pay was good, but she had her eye on marketing. So much so that she willingly took a pay cut to move into sales, waking up early to learn the ropes from merchandisers and store personnel.
“There is no shame in starting at the bottom,” she recalled in a 2023 graduation speech she delivered at the UP Virata School of Business.

blocks.caption: ALMA MATER. Sazon takes a selfie with the 2023 graduating class of the UP Virata School of Business. Photo from Sazon’s LinkedIn.

blocks.text: From there came stints at Del Monte and GlaxoSmithKline, working across food, pharmaceuticals, and personal care, before she spent 12 years at Globe. She rose through the ranks managing its postpaid, small-business, and broadband operations. By the time then-Globe chief Ernest Cu tapped her to lead Mynt in 2020, she had a marketer’s understanding of Filipino consumers and a telco veteran’s discipline in delivering products to them fast.
Fintech, however, is a different beast.

Finance and technology weren’t exactly her specialties, and taking over a company in the middle of lockdowns — without even meeting much of the team in person — was hardly an inviting prospect. But the timing couldn’t have been better for GCash. With the pandemic raging, Filipinos suddenly needed ways to pay bills, move money, and shop without handling cash.

Those who’ve complained about GCash’s demanding work culture might find Sazon’s talk of an “obsession” with solving customer problems and setting ever-higher targets painfully familiar. But the growth is hard to dispute. By June 2026, GCash had 41.5 million monthly active users.

And the personal accolades have followed. Sazon made it into Forbes’ 2026 50 Over 50 Global list and Fortune’s Asia’s 100 Most Powerful Women, ranking 35th, up two spots from 2025 and the highest among Filipinas.
Now that Mynt has reached this milestone, where does Sazon take it next?
“Becoming a public company is not the finish line,” she told the crowd at the PSE. (READ: On day one, rush for GCash IPO shares briefly trips up trading systems)

blocks.caption: After the IPO party, GCash comes for 5-6 lending next

blocks.text: The ambition is to make the fintech superapp’s lending services as big a revenue contributor as payments. In the first half of 2026, the split was 43% to 57%, respectively. Mynt is now allocating 60% of its nearly P10 billion in net fresh IPO proceeds to expand its loan portfolio over the next few years.

Executives explained much of this to reporters at the post-listing media briefing — that is, executives with the conspicuous exception of Sazon herself. Word has it Bloomberg got first dibs on the CEO, who was whisked away for the interview right after the listing ceremony.

“With regards to the stock performance, it’s encouraging to see early gains, and hopefully, we are able to sustain it and even see an increase later in the day,” she told Bloomberg TV, all smiles as GCash shares traded about 1.5% above their offer price at the time.
The market, as always, is unknowable.

After briefly reaching P6.76, GCash finished its debut at P6.60, precisely where it started, before sliding down to P6.27 to close its first week of trading. Investment bank UBS, the IPO’s stabilizing agent, has a P7.95-billion stabilization fund to snap up shares and cushion declines below P6.60 until mid-November. But even with that much firepower, there’s only so much it can do to keep the stock from falling.
For now, the fintech queen’s newly public fortune is at the mercy of the market. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Democrat James Talarico targets Elon Musk at rally: ‘Texas is not for sale’
articles.summary:
The Senate candidate denounced opponent Ken Paxton, calling out corruption allegations and support from Musk

James Talarico, the Democratic candidate for the US Senate in Texas, has taken…

blocks.text: James Talarico, the Democratic candidate for the US Senate in Texas, has taken aim at Elon Musk, warning that the tech mogul is trying to buy political influence and declaring: “Texas is not for sale.”

Talarico held a campaign rally on Friday at the University of Texas at Austin, packing an auditorium at his alma mater with hundreds of students and other supporters, who cheered, whooped and waved campaign signs.

The Presbyterian seminarian’s insurgent run against Texas attorney general Ken Paxton – a staunch ally of Donald Trump – has become one of the most closely watched races in next month’s midterm elections to decide control of Congress. Democrats are seeking their first statewide win since 1994.

Talarico, 37, struck his usual upbeat message on Friday but also pulled no punches in denouncing Paxton – who was impeached by his own party over corruption accusations and had a very public divorce – as the most corrupt politician in the state’s history.

“I have a legislative record; Ken Paxton has a criminal record,” said Talarico, a state representative, wearing a dark blue jacket, white open collar shirt and blue jeans. “This election is about whether you want a senator who puts money in your pocket or who puts money in their own. This election is about whether you want a senator who is for Texas or for himself. This election is about whether you want senator who serves you or serves their billionaire mega donors.”

blocks.caption: People hold signs supporting James Talarico at a rally in Temple, Texas on Friday. Photograph: Joel Angel Juarez/Reuters

blocks.text: Paxton, he continued, has the ultimate mega donor. “Elon Musk is trying to buy the Senate seat. We just found out that the richest man in the world is almost single-handedly bankrolling this effort to install Ken Paxton in the US Senate and stop the movement that we are building in our state.

“In all likelihood, if you’ve seen an attack ad on your screens, that was Elon. If you’ve gotten lies in your mailbox, that was Elon. If you received a text message saying scary things about me with scary black and white photos, that was Elon too.”

Speaking against the backdrop of a giant Texan state flag and 40 young supporters holding “Talarico” signs, the Democrat said that, where his movement is funded by 1.3 million individuals, Paxton is funded by “one dude”.

In a state where data centres have become an incendiary issue, Talarico said: “Elon Musk wants our land. He wants our water. He wants our tax dollars. He wants his very own personal United States senator. He is trying to buy Texas. But on November 3rd, we are going to deliver a crystal clear message to the world’s first trillionaire: Texas is not for sale.”

Musk, who lives in Texas and has relocated SpaceX, Tesla, X and other businesses there, has contributed $158m to the Senate Leadership Fund, which in turn transferred the same amount to Texas PAC, a Republican super PAC supporting Paxton, according to federal filings.

Talarico has offset the outside-spending disadvantage with grassroots fundraising. His campaign says it raised $64m from July through September, more than triple Paxton’s total, with 97% of donations under $100 each.

Talarico told the crowd that super PACs and “billionaire mega-donors” are spending $200m in the most expensive Senate race in US history to defeat his grassroots campaign. “Big money is powerful, but it is nothing compared to people power,” he insisted, invoking biblical imagery comparing his supporters to “the slingshot” that David used to defeat Goliath

blocks.caption: James Talarico addresses supporters at a campaign rally in Temple, Texas. Photograph: Joel Angel Juarez/Reuters

blocks.text: Talarico’s rally capped a turbulent month in what has emerged as America’s biggest battleground state. Talarico fell ill with the flu at the end of September and was not seen in public for nine days.

At a rally in San Antonio, Texas, Donald Trump claimed without evidence that “Tala-freako”, as he nicknames the Democrat, is vegan and had fallen ill because he tried eating meat for political purposes. That quickly metastasised into an online rumour that Talarico had checked into a mental health facility in Ohio. It was comprehensively debunked.

Meanwhile the Wall Street Journal published a video showing Paxton celebrating New Year’s Eve in Dubai with two US fugitives, Anosh Ahmed and Sameer Suhail, who were indicted in Illinois on healthcare-fraud charges. Ahmed donated $190,000 to Paxton, including $25,000 after his indictment.
Back on the campaign trail, Talarico set out on a “Clear Eyes, Full Hearts” tour of the state. He held a CNN town hall with sceptical Republicans and independent voters.

Paxton, meanwhile, launched an 18-day bus tour of Texas. His message was aimed at conservative voters with the slogan “Come and Take It”, an attack on what he called the far left. Republicans sought to tie Talarico with positions on transgender issues that have proved potent in conservative campaigning.

The campaign entered its final stretch with the Democrat holding a narrow polling advantage. The RealClearPolitics average for polls conducted from 6 to 19 October put Talarico ahead by 1.8 percentage points. An Emerson College Polling/ Nexstar Media survey released on Thursday found that 48% of voters support Talarico while 46% favour Paxton.
Early voting began on 19 October, giving both campaigns an immediate test of their ability to mobilise supporters. Talarico voted earlier on Friday.

Supporters at Friday’s rally expressed growing frustration with incumbent Republican officials such as Paxton along with optimism that Talarico’s message could signal a new political era for the Lone Star State.

blocks.caption: James Talarico greets supporters during a campaign rally. Photograph: Joel Angel Juarez/Reuters

blocks.text: Alina Anil, a 19-year-old student at the University of Texas, who had already cast her ballot, said she attended the event to see Talarico in person and demonstrate her support.

“We’ve been red for a long time and nothing has really come out of it,” Anil said. “As a student, I don’t think there’s been a lot of changes in Texas. We need some change and James Talarico seems promising. He was a teacher before, so I have faith in that and I have faith in him.”

Dakota Walker, 31, a pediatric physical therapist, arrived wearing a custom T-shirt reading “Talafrico: Talarico refreshing for Texas”, in the style of the Topo-Chico brand of sparkling mineral water.
“What’s not to like about him, what’s not to love about him, honestly?” Walker said. “He has morals, he has values, he’s an overall good human being and I think we need a drastic change.

“I have to spend so much of my time fighting for my kids, making sure that they get what they need when a family with a child with a disability or different abilities shouldn’t have to do that. I know we need healthcare reform and he is very big on that.”
Texas Democrats have had their hopes dashed before, notably when former congressman Beto O’Rourke lost a race to Republican Sen. Ted Cruz in 2018 by less than 3 percentage points.
Asked what a Democratic statewide victory would mean, Walker replied: “Oh man, I’ll probably cry, honestly. We need a lot of change and I feel like it’s time for a new era.”

Patrick Pearson, 46, an assistive technology professional, said he wanted to back Talarico because of his commitment to policy change. “From everything I’ve read about him and heard, I think he sounds really awesome,” Pearson said. “He’s actually trying to make a change and has a very positive message.”

articles.title: OpenAI resumes frontier AI training after security overhaul, discloses flaw in widely used software
articles.summary: The disclosure comes amid concerns over the ability of increasingly capable AI agents to identify and exploit software flaws, including in the guardrails meant to contain them

blocks.text: OPENAI. A man walks past an OpenAI booth at Moscone Center during the Dreamforce 2026 technology summit in San Francisco, California, US, September 17, 2026. REUTERS/Carlos Barria/File Photo
Carlos Barria/Reuters
The disclosure comes amid concerns over the ability of increasingly capable AI agents to identify and exploit software flaws, including in the guardrails meant to contain them

items: OpenAI resumed training its advanced AI models after tightening security and addressing a flaw in the Brotli data compression tool, which could allow attackers to execute malicious code.
The company paused training following an incident where a research model gained limited internet access due to a configuration error, using the time to strengthen defenses.
AI safety evaluators found new vulnerabilities in OpenAI's internal systems, which the company claims to have patched, although the evaluators have not verified these fixes.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

OpenAI said on Friday, October 23, it had resumed training of its most advanced AI models after tightening security and barring internet access, and disclosed a flaw in a widely used software that it found while testing its defenses.
The disclosure comes amid concerns over the ability of increasingly capable AI agents to identify and exploit software flaws, including in the guardrails meant to contain them.

OpenAI had paused training of its most capable models after one of its research models used a configuration error to gain limited internet access in September. The company said it contained the incident and used the pause to strengthen its defenses.

To test them, OpenAI had teams of AI agents try to break out of their restricted environments. It said the agents found previously unknown flaws, which it had fixed, and training resumed on October 1.
During that exercise, the ChatGPT maker found a flaw in Brotli, a widely used data compression tool.

The company said attackers could exploit the flaw by sending malicious data that lets them run their own code on affected systems, including those using popular web software such as Node.js, Bun and Envoy.

OpenAI said the root cause was fixed in Brotli’s source code in February, before it was known to create a security vulnerability, but no new version was released at the time. Brotli has since released updated versions and published a public record of the flaw after OpenAI disclosed it.

Separately on Thursday, AI safety evaluators METR and Redwood Research said they found several new vulnerabilities in OpenAI’s internal system, including an exploit agents could have used to keep hundreds of their actions from being monitored, in a pilot review earlier this year.
OpenAI told the safety organizations it has since patched all vulnerabilities affecting its production safeguards, although METR and Redwood said they had not verified the fixes.

OpenAI has been conducting a broad review of its AI models’ activity since the Hugging Face incident in July, and has informed more than 100 organizations about incidents of unauthorized activity tied to its AI agents. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Hitler's Eagle's Nest retreat catches fire, police say
articles.summary: Authorities have arrested a suspect as firemen try to put out the fire in Bavaria, near the Austrian border.

image.caption: The site once housed the Nazi leader's heavily fortified country residence [FILE: Jun 21, 2004]Image: Peter Kneffel/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: A fire broke out at the Kehlsteinhaus retreat, more commonly known as Adolf Hitler's Eagle's Nest, on Friday evening, Bavarian police said.
The Kehlsteinhaus was engulfed in flames, a police statement read, adding that a suspect has been arrested and the incident was being criminally investigated.
What do we know so far about the Kehlsteinhaus fire?
A fire alarm went off at the Kehlsteinhaus on the Obersalzberg in Berchtesgaden at around 9:15 p.m. local time (1915 GMT) on Friday, the police said in a statement.
"The fire brigades, who were alerted immediately, could already see flames clearly visible at the Kehlsteinhaus as they approached," the police statement read.
Firefighters struggled to reach the Kehlsteinhaus, which sits at some 1,834 meters (6,017 feet) above sea level, with their engines.
Police added that the building and its immediate vicinity could only be entered while wearing respiratory protective equipment (RPE).
Police said they were unaware of any injuries as of yet.
The site once housed Hitler's heavily fortified country residence, where he is believed to have partially written his book "Mein Kampf."
It remains a symbol of the Nazi regime and is among only a few monuments of the Hitler era that survived the World War II bombing unscathed. Today, it is home to a popular restaurant.

articles.title: DepEd using data-driven criteria in determining classroom allocation --Angara
articles.summary: The Department of Education is using data-driven criteria in its construction strategy to determine classroom allocations according to school needs, DepEd Secretary Sonny Angara said.

blocks.text: Published October 24, 2026 10:37am
The Department of Education is using data-driven criteria in its construction strategy to determine classroom allocations according to school needs, DepEd Secretary Sonny Angara said.

Angara made the statement as he acknowledged the report of the Second Congressional Commission on Education (EDCOM 2) on gaps in allocations for local government units (LGUs) with the highest estimated classroom shortages based on initial 2026 allocations.

The Education department said its classroom needs assessment and validated school-site priorities serve as basis for identifying projects to implement, including those through partnerships with qualified LGUs, as per DepEd Memorandum No. 038, s. 2026.

“We share the same mission with EDCOM. Through strategic partnerships with qualified LGUs, we ensure that resources go directly to where our schools and learners need them most,” Angara said Thursday.

“Ang alokasyon natin para sa mga silid-aralan ay dapat direktang tumutugon sa mga eskwelahang pinakamatindi ang pangangailangan. Kailangan naka-base sa tunay na datos ang ating mga desisyon para bawat pisong inilalaan natin, tunay na nararamdaman sa ating mga paaralan," he said.
(Our allocations for classrooms should directly meet the needs of schools with the greatest needs. Our decisions should be based on valid data so each peso allocated will be felt in our schools.)
DepEd said they will continue to weigh the severity of shortages, site readiness, project feasibility, and implementation timelines in deciding on classroom allocations.

It is deploying a multi-pronged strategy integrating Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH)-led construction, LGU partnerships, Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs), DepEd Learning Continuity Spaces (LCS),and collaborative initiatives with both government and private sector organizations.
The DepEd said allocations cover 439 LGUs, 1,955 schools, and 8,777 classrooms nationwide under the current LGU-led classroom construction initiative.

"This infrastructure rollout spans 81 provincial LGUs accounting for 4,043 classrooms across 1,022 schools, 127 city LGUs covering 3,123 classrooms across 468 schools, and 231 municipal LGUs encompassing 1,611 classrooms across 465 schools," it added.
DepEd also had agreements with Philippine Amusement and Gaming Corporation (PAGCOR) and 48 LGUs which led to 576 classrooms to be built in priority communities.

The department said it requires regular physical and financial progress reporting, technical validation, and monitoring protocols across division, regional, and central office levels to strengthen transparency and accountability.

“To truly deliver for our learners, we need a transparent and evidence-based approach. It is the only way to ensure that available resources are directly translated into classrooms where they are needed the most,” Angara said. —KG, GMA News

articles.title: In new ICC request, prosecutors cite 'orders from above,' reward in Duterte case
articles.summary: ICC prosecutors are seeking to admit three additional witness accounts describing alleged orders, planning and payments linked to killings.

blocks.text: October 24, 2026 | 10:35am

ICC Senior Trial Lawyer Julian Nicholls looks on during a preliminary hearing of former President Rodrigo Duterte at the International Criminal Court (ICC) in The Hague on September 16, 2026, during a preparatory session as he faces charges over his “war on drugs,” which killed thousands.
Piroschka Van de Wouw, pool via AFP

MANILA, Philippines — International Criminal Court (ICC) prosecutors are seeking to present testimony describing alleged orders "from above," planning and payments tied to killings in their crimes against humanity case against former president Rodrigo Duterte.

In a redacted filing released Friday, October 23, the ICC Office of the Prosecutor asked Trial Chamber III to admit the previously recorded testimonies of three witnesses identified only as P-1155, P-1156 and P-1157.
Prosecutors said the witnesses could provide evidence under Count 3 of the case, which covers murder and attempted murder allegations, including Duterte's alleged knowledge and intent.
They could also point to the existence of a policy to "neutralize" suspected criminals through violence, prosecutors argued.
Witness P-1155's account covers alleged orders "from above," instructions given to police officers and a reward linked to one of the incidents under examination, according to the prosecution.
The testimony of P-1156, meanwhile, concerns alleged orders, planning, preparations and payment related to the killings.
The third witness, P-1157, is expected to provide evidence concerning a killing and a planned police operation against the targets.

An earlier prosecution filing, made public on October 21, also sought the admission of recorded testimonies from three other witnesses, identified as P-0008, P-1164 and P-1303. Prosecutors said their accounts could help establish a pattern of police killings.
Recorded testimony
The prosecution argued that the three accounts were consistent and corroborated one another.
The testimonies, moreover, would establish the alleged policy of targeting suspected criminals through violent acts, including murder, it said.

The previously recorded accounts were requested to be admitted under Rule 68(3) of the ICC Rules of Procedure and Evidence, a procedure that allows qualifying prior testimony to be introduced at trial.
The prosecution maintained that admitting the previous statements would help shorten the proceedings without prejudicing Duterte's right to challenge the evidence against him.
Expert report
In a separate filing released October 23, prosecutors also sought the admission of an expert report and 15 associated items from a witness identified as P-1400.

The expert's field and much of the report's contents were redacted. Prosecutors proposed shortening the witness's direct examination from five hours to two hours while allowing further questioning in court.
The ICC has scheduled another status conference for November 2 to address outstanding preparations ahead of the trial.
The ICC's Trial Chamber III, presided over by Judge Joanna Korner, is expected to rule on the latest requests.
Trial opening. Duterte's trial is set to open on November 30 over crimes against humanity charges involving killings during his presidency and his tenure as Davao City mayor.
Duterte has been detained in The Hague since March 2025.

Earlier classified as a super typhoon and one of the strongest storms in the ⁠Pacific this year, Champi was still packing gusts of about 126km per hour (78 miles per hour) near its ⁠centre, according to Taiwan’s Central Weather Administration (CWA).
The storm was about ​150km (93 miles) east ‌of Taiwan, the CWA ‌said, having glanced off the island’s northeast coast in the early ‌hours of Saturday.

blocks.caption: Waves generated by Typhoon Champi crash against a seawall in Keelung. Photograph: Ann Wang/Reuters

Large parts of northern and central Taiwan, including Taipei, declared a second ​day of ‌office and ​school closures ​on Saturday, and some flights were still being cancelled.

articles.title: 7 dead, 40 wounded after gunmen open fire during funeral at Greek Orthodox church in Jordan
articles.summary: Gunmen opened fire during a funeral at a church in Jordan on Friday, killing seven people and wounding 40 others, authorities said.

image.caption: A man looks through a gap in a stone wall, toward a church in Karak, Jordan, where a shooting occurred at a funeral held there hours earlier on Friday. (The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World·New
Gunmen opened fire during a funeral at a church in Jordan on Friday, killing seven people and wounding 40 others, authorities said.
Gunfire erupted roughly 15 minutes after funeral started, witness says
The shooting took place at a Greek Orthodox church in Karak, about 180 kilometres south of the capital, Amman.

Footage broadcast on Jordanian state television showed two gunmen, apparently armed with pistols, approaching the church and firing shots. A third man, apparently carrying a semi-automatic rifle, then approached and fired before all three ran toward the church.
Video taken by witnesses showed broken glass and pools of blood on the church floor.
Unclear if any gunmen captured, killed
Dorgham Halasa, who was among the mourners inside the church, said intense gunfire erupted about 15 minutes after the funeral began and people started running.
"It was a weird situation, and heavy gunfire," Halasa said.

He did not see the gunmen but said other people reported seeing four of them. The Associated Press could not independently verify the number of assailants, and Jordan's security services did not immediately release details.
Gendarmerie forces are seen standing guard outside Al-Karak Government Hospital, where some of the injured persons are being treated. (Alaa Al-Sukhni/Reuters)

A government statement said that the attack was "carried out by unknown assailants" but did not say whether any gunmen had been captured or killed. It said "investigations are underway at full speed."
Jordan declared three days of national mourning, according to the kingdom's Petra News Agency.
Karak is home to a minority Christian population.

In 2016, gunmen ambushed police in a series of attacks in Karak, including at a Crusader castle popular with tourists, killing 10 people, including seven officers and a Canadian tourist, and wounding dozens. Jordanian security forces killed those gunmen after a long standoff.
2 people in critical condition
Jordan's Health Minister Ibrahim al-Budour said two of the wounded are in critical condition.
A view of the interior of the church is seen, through a shattered window, on Friday. (The Associated Press)

King Abdullah II said on X that Jordan "will confront the terrorist act that targeted Karak with the harshest penalties" and offered his "deepest condolences to the families of the martyrs, and our wishes for recovery to the wounded."

Jordan's Prime Minister Jafar Hassan said during a security meeting in Karak on Friday evening that the attack was the result of terrorist ideology and blind extremism. He said the assailants would be punished and legal measures taken against those who seek to introduce extremism.
Condemnation of the killings came from around the region, including from Lebanon, Syria, Egypt and Oman.
Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein called his Jordanian counterpart and "affirmed Iraq's solidarity with Jordan in the face of terrorism," Hussein's office said in a statement.
UN Secretary-General António Guterres condemned the attack during a funeral as "especially heinous," spokesman Stéphane Dujarric said.
"The secretary-general also calls for all those responsible to be found and to be held to account."

articles.title: California officials ordered by DoJ to set aside ‘likely’ noncitizen ballots
articles.summary:
Letters from federal prosecutors represent latest escalation as Trump continues to make claims of voter fraud

Federal prosecutors sent letters to county registrars across California on…

blocks.text: Federal prosecutors sent letters to county registrars across California on Friday demanding that local officials set aside and verify ballots that the Department of Justice said may belong to noncitizens, according to the Los Angeles county registrar and a letter obtained by the Associated Press.

The letters are the latest escalation in a legal battle between California and Donald Trump’s Department of Justice, which has recently focused on the state in its efforts to root out noncitizen voting ahead of the midterm elections.
Data shows illegal voting by people who are not US citizens is incredibly rare, difficult to prove and has not been shown to change the outcome of races.

Earlier this month, the federal government targeted Los Angeles county and the California secretary of state’s office in a lawsuit that aimed to block them from counting the votes of roughly 20,000 people who are “likely” noncitizen voters. A hearing on the case is scheduled for Tuesday.
The Trump administration asked the ninth circuit court of appeals to rule on the lawsuit barring a decision from the district judge assigned to the case. They set a deadline for Saturday.
Now, according to the LA county registrar’s office, at least 18 counties across the state have received similar letters.

They have been given a 48-hour deadline to provide identifying information corresponding with ballots that the federal government believes were sent to noncitizens illegally registered to vote. The letter requests that county officials also sequester any ballots where citizenship cannot be verified.
“Any election official who knowingly processes the ballot of a noncitizen is opening themselves to legal jeopardy,” said first assistant US attorney Bill Essayli.
The justice department is asking counties to send information about the voters it suspects are noncitizens including social security numbers, ID information, a copy of their registration and more.

That information can help the government and state quickly assess each person suspected of illegally registering to vote, said the letter sent to San Bernardino County voting officials. The letter says the government’s list of suspected noncitizen voters includes 1,133 people from the inland southern California county.

California’s secretary of state and the Los Angeles county registrar have opposed the federal government’s demands. In legal filings, lawyers for California say the request threatens to delay the certification of the vote and undermine the legitimacy of the November midterms. They have also argued that the federal government’s data is unreliable and that their demands risk disenfranchisement of citizens.

Voting is under way in California, with the state’s more than 23 million registered voters receiving ballots in the mail earlier this month. The state said in legal filings that over 330,000 mail-in ballots have already been counted.

The letters on Friday came on the heels of statewide sweep by federal authorities earlier in the week, where 28 people from the list of 20,000 were charged with illegally registering to vote. Some were also charged with illegally voting and lying on naturalization paperwork. Those charges could lead to years in prison.

articles.title: How a Dubai trip to see his mom launched a film career
articles.summary: James Durias Arieta came to Dubai with no plan other than to be with his ‘TNT’ mother, a visit that unexpectedly launched his career in cinematography

blocks.text: James Durias Arieta came to Dubai with no plan other than to be with his ‘TNT’ mother, a visit that unexpectedly launched his career in cinematography

items: James Durias Arieta moved to Dubai to reunite with his mother, who was an undocumented worker, and faced challenges growing up without her support.
After initially working as a procurement officer, Arieta rediscovered his passion for photography, overcoming rejections and gaining recognition in the industry.
He eventually opened his own creative agency in 2024 and is now focused on mentoring aspiring cinematographers while his mother continues to work abroad.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
DUBAI, United Arab Emirates – He came to Dubai to visit the mother he had not seen in ages. Years later, he would become a renowned cinematographer running his own creative agency in UAE.

It was a big leap, but that’s just how it has been for 33-year-old James Durias Arieta. He originally arrived here to see his mom, Preciousa, who at the time was an undocumented worker making ends meet, trying to send money home.

“Since Grade 1, around six years old po ako, hanggang college hindi kami nagkita,” Arieta shared. “Hindi nya pa ako ma-sponsoran kasi TNT (tago nang tago) siya dito sa Dubai — one of the reasons din kung bakit hindi siya maka-uwi. Mas pinili nya na mag-stay dito sa Dubai for us, may maipadala.”

(From Grade 1, when I was around six years old, up to college, I never saw her. She could not sponsor me because she was overstaying — one of the reasons why she could not go home. She chose to stay here in Dubai for us, to keep sending money.)

Living without a mother was tough, said Arieta. To help cover school fees and daily expenses, he and his siblings sold eggs and newspapers in the morning, and pork at night — at times working from 11 pm to 5 am.
“It taught me how to survive at a young age,” he said.
He was unable to finish college because what his mother sent home was only enough for food, and his father was not earning a regular income.
“I could not sustain payments for school fees and the transportation,” said Arieta, who was taking up civil engineering at the University of Mindanao.
Eventually, his mother was able to send him to Dubai through a tourist visa, though there was no assurance he wouldn’t be offloaded at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport (NAIA).

“Salamat at nakapasok naman,” Arieta said. “Bisita lang sana ako, to see my mother’s situation. Wala po talaga akong plan, pero ayun, two weeks remaining ng visa nag-decide ako na mag-work at samahan ang nanay ko since nakita ko sitwasyon. Luckily, nakahanap agad ng trabaho.”

(Thankfully, I got in. I was really only visiting my mother, to see her situation. I did not plan to stay long, but with two weeks remaining on my visa, I decided to work and stay with my mother after seeing her situation. Luckily, I found a job right away.)
That first job was as a procurement officer for a construction company.
To save money, they stayed in Sharjah, a city neighboring Dubai to the north. There, his mother managed to run an apartment unit where they occupied a single room, renting out the rest to others.
But just as Arieta was settling into his new life, his mother had to surrender to authorities and be flown home to the Philippines because her own mother was hospitalized.
Left on his own, life as a photographer — his first love — slowly seeped back into Arieta. He began spending his weekends wandering around the city, shooting everything he saw.
“Marami rin akong pinagdaanang rejections. Minsan bina-block pa nga ako kasi makulit talaga ako magtanong sa mga veteran sa industry. Pero malaking part din yun ng learning process ko,” said Arieta.
(I went through a lot of rejections. Sometimes, I even got blocked because I was so persistent with my questions to veterans in the industry. But it was a big part of my learning process.)

Eventually, he started reaping what he sowed. His work was recognized at the Doha Photography Festival in Qatar, and he was later invited as a guest speaker at a Nikon launch event in Karachi, Pakistan, where he moved the audience with his life journey. Capping it all off, he became a “who’s who” in the regional creative industry.
It did not stop there. In 2024, he opened his own creative agency, handling commercial campaigns and visual storytelling for major companies.
“Doha was my first workshop outside the country under Nikon. I was also recognized there as an aspiring trainer for the region,” he shared.

“Karachi was a bigger event with about 700 attendees. It was a cinema setup and my video was the first to flash on the screen. I received really good feedback. Right after that, I was given an award,” added Arieta, who was officially taken on by Nikon as one of its regional trainers last year.
“We have workshops almost every weekend. For me personally, most of the time, I hold workshops around twice a month.”
Today, Arieta is focused on passing his learnings down to aspiring cinematographers in the region.

And his mother? They say you can take the worker out of the country, but you can’t take the hustle out of an overseas Filipino worker (OFW). True to form, Preciousa is back on the move — this time, working in Saudi Arabia. – Rappler.com

Gunmen opened fire during a funeral at a church in Jordan on…

The shooting took place at a Greek Orthodox church in Karak, about 180km (110 miles) south of the capital, Amman.

Footage broadcast on Jordanian state television showed two gunmen who appear to be holding pistols approaching the church and firing shots. A third man who appears to be holding a semiautomatic rifle then approaches and opens fire, and all three then run toward the church.

Dorgham Halasa, who was among the mourners inside the church, said intense gunfire erupted 15 minutes after the funeral had started, and then people started running. “It was a weird situation, and heavy gunfire,” Halasa said.

He did not see the gunmen, but said other people reported seeing four of them. The Associated Press could not independently verify the number of assailants, and Jordan’s security services did not immediately release details.

Jordan declared three days of national mourning, according to the kingdom’s Petra news agency.
Karak is home to a minority Christian population.

In 2016, gunmen ambushed police in a series of attacks in Karak, including at a Crusader castle popular with tourists, killing 10 people, including seven officers, and wounding dozens. Jordanian security forces killed those gunmen after a long standoff.
Jordan’s health minister Ibrahim al-Budour said two of those wounded are in critical condition.

articles.title: 'Rosal' to exit PAR Saturday morning after loop east of Taiwan
articles.summary: The typhoon looped east of Taiwan as Batanes remained under Signal No. 1.

blocks.text: October 24, 2026 | 9:25am
Relative position of cyclone Rosal as of 5 a.m. on Saturday, Oct. 24, 2026 as seen in a satellite-based rendering from PAGASA.
PAGASA

MANILA, Philippines — Typhoon Rosal is forecast to exit the Philippine area of responsibility Saturday morning, October 24 after making a counterclockwise loop over the sea east of Taiwan, PAGASA said.
In its 5 a.m. bulletin on October 24, the state weather bureau said Rosal had weakened slightly and was moving southwestward at 10 kilometers per hour.
As of 4 a.m., the center of the typhoon was estimated 420 kilometers north of Itbayat, Batanes.
Rosal had maximum sustained winds of 150 kph near the center, gusts of up to 185 kph and a central pressure of 955 hectopascals.
Strong to typhoon-force winds extended as far as 850 kilometers from its center.
Batanes under Signal No. 1
Tropical Cyclone Wind Signal No. 1 remained in effect over Batanes, where strong winds of 39 to 61 kph may be experienced.
PAGASA said minimal to minor impacts from strong winds are possible in areas under Signal No. 1.

The periphery of Rosal may also bring strong to gale-force gusts Saturday over the Babuyan Islands, Ilocos Norte, Aurora, northern Quezon, Polillo Islands, Bicol Region, Romblon, Capiz, Iloilo and Negros Occidental.
Strong to gale-force gusts may affect Batanes and the Babuyan Islands on Sunday.
Dangerous seas over Northern Luzon
A gale warning remained in effect over the seaboards of Northern Luzon.
Very rough seas with waves reaching as high as 5.5 meters are forecast over the seaboards of Batanes, while waves may reach 4.5 meters along the northern seaboard of the Babuyan Islands.
PAGASA warned that sea travel is risky for vessels of all types and tonnage in these areas.

Rough seas are also forecast over several coastal waters of Northern Luzon, with waves ranging from 3 to 4 meters in parts of the Babuyan Islands, Cagayan, Ilocos Norte, Ilocos Sur, Pangasinan, Isabela, northern Aurora and Catanduanes.
Mariners of small sea vessels, including motorbancas, were advised not to venture out under these conditions.
Rosal to weaken further
PAGASA forecasts the typhoon will leave PAR Saturday morning and head toward the East China Sea.
It is then expectef to gradually accelerate north-northeastward after completing its loop east of Taiwan.
Rosal is also forecast to gradually weaken over the next 12 hours before weakening more rapidly over the East China Sea.
It may be downgraded to a severe tropical storm by Sunday, PAGASA said.

articles.title: Embattled Greens senator Jordon Steele-John confirms leave from parliament after allegations against him made public
articles.summary:
WA politician says he considered attending Senate estimates virtually but was told it would be ‘unacceptable’

  • Get our

blocks.text: Jordon Steele-John has confirmed he will not attend parliament next week as the embattled Greens senator releases a letter detailing the allegations against him.
After days of confusion following historical complaints about alleged misconduct were publicly aired in the media, Steele-John posted a statement to social media late Friday night.

In the statement, the Western Australian senator said he considered attending Senate estimates virtually but was told it would be “unacceptable”. He will instead focus on seeing through an independent investigation to its conclusion, he said.

“Over the past few days there has been a growing chorus calling on me not to attend parliament next week. I have explored attending digitally but have been informed that would also be unacceptable,” Steele-John said.
Steele-John said a precedent of keeping parliamentarians out of parliament after “allegations of allegations” are made had now been set.
“Had an allegation or complaint been made against me, I would have taken these actions immediately,” he said.

The 32-year-old senator’s attendance in parliament for the remainder of the year had been uncertain after a public stoush with the party’s leader, David Shoebridge, over whether he was on leave while an investigation was undertaken into allegations he had acted inappropriately towards women between 2017 and 2025.
The complaints are now subject to an independent investigation commissioned by the WA Greens and have been referred to the Independent Parliamentary Standards Commission.
Shoebridge claimed Steele-John had requested leave and he accepted it last week after seven party members penned a letter to the leader urging an investigation into the claims.

The three-page letter sent on 13 October, and first published by the Nine newspapers, said the authors had been “made aware of multiple allegations of serious misconduct” against Steele-John about his “behaviour in the presence of women”.
The letter referred to an allegation of sexual harassment at a Greens campaign event in 2024 that the alleged victim had not reported out of fear and backlash. The letter provided no further detail.
In another, the authors referred to an allegation of “serious sexual misconduct” in 2025.
Also contained in the letter was a reference to a disparaging nickname for Steele-John – “feels on wheels” – which the authors said implied he had a reputation for acting inappropriately.

“To be clear, all signatories to this letter know that an allegation does not equate to a fact and/or guilt. We simply believe that it is in the party’s best interests to ensure that every allegation is investigated thoroughly, in alignment with community and member expectations,” the letter’s authors wrote.

Steele-John was defiant in a lengthy statement last Sunday, rejecting the allegations against him, denying he agreed to take leave from parliament and accusing an internal faction within the Greens of playing “nasty political games” in their decision to release the letter to the media.

Steele-John said any claims of his alleged behaviour should be investigated “fairly and thoroughly” but accused an “unofficial faction” within the WA branch had released the complaint letter to the media in a bid to oust him from the Senate.
Guardian Australia has confirmed the WA police told Steele-John the investigation was closed in May with no charges.

articles.title: Helen Haines’s condition improves days after losing both legs from alleged attack
articles.summary:
Independent MP now serious but stable, according to update from Melbourne’s Alfred hospital

  • Get our breaking news…

blocks.text: Independent MP Helen Haines’s condition has been downgraded to serious but stable after she lost both legs following an alleged attack near her electorate office in north-east Victoria on Monday afternoon.
The Alfred hospital in Melbourne provided an update on Haines’s condition on Saturday morning.
“The patient is in a serious but stable condition at The Alfred on Saturday morning,” a spokesperson for the hospital said.

Haines, the federal MP for the Victorian seat of Indi, had been in a critical but stable condition after she was struck by a car in Wangaratta on Monday afternoon. Surgeons were trying to save her right leg on Tuesday, but both legs had to be amputated due to the seriousness of her injuries.

Police on Tuesday charged Brendan Nugent, 43, from nearby Tarrawingee with dangerous driving causing serious injury, intentionally cause serious injury and the commonwealth offence of causing harm to a commonwealth public official. Police have since charged him with two additional offences – cultivating and possessing cannabis – according to court documents.
Nugent appeared in court on Wednesday and did not apply for bail.
On Friday, an update on Haines’s social media accounts said her staff were working to reopen her electorate offices next Thursday.
“What happened on Monday has deeply affected Helen’s family and all of her staff. Many of us witnessed the incident and some were among the first to come to her aid,” the post read.

“As Helen takes the time she needs to recover, we will take time to look after ourselves and one another, too. Healing will take time, and we ask for your understanding as we navigate the days and weeks ahead.”
The alleged attack on Haines has reverberated through Australian politics, prompting conversations about the temperature of political debate and mental services in regional Victoria.

articles.title: Rubio tells Cubans ‘now is the time’ to act to see political change
articles.summary:
US secretary of state makes comments after Trump tells US rally warships could intervene on return from Iran

Marco Rubio urged Cubans seeking political change in their country to act, saying…

blocks.text: Marco Rubio urged Cubans seeking political change in their country to act, saying “now is the time” moments after Donald Trump told a Friday rally for candidates in south Florida that US warships could intervene in Cuba on their way back from the Iran war.

The US secretary of state, in his social media post addressed “to those who seek to create positive change”, urged Cubans to capitalize on Trump’s plans. “The disappointment of failed promises, corruption, and the privileged lives of only a few; seize this opportunity to create the change you desire through a discrete [sic] partnership with the CIA,” Rubio said.

The top US diplomat, whose parents left Cuba for the United States before the socialist revolution there, seemed to mistakenly use the word “discrete”, meaning separate, rather than “discreet”, meaning private or secret.

Trump first floated this idea earlier this year, but has not mentioned it in recent months. But he revived it in response to a shouted question from the crowd about the island nation. He was campaigning just days before midterm elections in which voters have expressed concern about the impact the US war on Iran has had on prices of goods from gas to groceries.

“We’ll do a little stopover,” Trump said. “Actually, what we’re going to do with Cuba is, we’re going to come back from Iran. Those beautiful ships will pass Cuba. We’ll have one of them stop about 50 yards off the coast. They’ll raise up their hands. And then we’re going to send Marco Rubio in to finish up the deal.”

Rubio and Trump have been bullish on action in Cuba, with Trump previously suggesting the country would “be next” in terms of intervention abroad, following the winding down of the Iran war he has long forecast but which has not yet happened.

In May, he and Rubio raised the specter of US military intervention in Cuba, a renewed threat that took on greater weight after the administration announced criminal charges against the island’s former leader, Raúl Castro. Trump told reporters in the Oval Office that previous US presidents had considered intervening in Cuba for decades but that “it looks like I’ll be the one that does it”.

Rubio told reporters separately that Cuba had been a national security threat for years because of its ties to US adversaries and that Trump was intent on addressing it. While saying the Trump administration wanted to resolve differences with Cuba peacefully, Rubio voiced doubts that the US could reach a diplomatic resolution with the island’s current government.
Rubio has not addressed Cuba in depth in public for several weeks, with his last comments coming in a 29 September interview with Fox News host Sean Hannity.

“The truth is Cuba has already fallen. It doesn’t have a functional economy and it’s governed by people who continue to preach about some revolution that has been dead for 20 years that’s never worked,” Rubio said, without alluding to any CIA operation.

“We are hopeful that Cuba will choose a different path. We are hopeful … that there will be some people in there that open their eyes to the reality of what they’re facing. We’re never going to allow Cuba to become a base of operation against American interests or pose a threat to our national security. On that we are abundantly clear.”

Rubio and other top Trump aides have met with Cuban officials in recent months to explore possible improvements in relations. But the US side has come away unimpressed from those talks, leading to even more sanctions imposed on the Cuban government.

During his address to the United Nations general assembly last month, Trump said Rubio – son of Cuban immigrants, who has long taken a hard line against Cuba’s socialist leadership – was “deep into negotiations with Cuba”, saying he would “not allow a haven for foreign adversaries to threaten America on our own doorstep”.
Days later, Trump told reporters that he anticipated that the two countries “will make a deal”, adding: “I don’t think we’ll need the military. Cuba is failing very badly.”

Earlier this week, the two countries clashed at the United Nations as the Trump administration sought once again to build opposition for an upcoming annual vote condemning Washington’s decades-long economic embargo against Havana.

Cuba has struggled since 2020 with an economic and energy crisis. Its gross domestic product has shrunk , and its 10 million residents have endured blackouts, food shortages and inflation. There have been waves of protests, and hundreds of thousands of Cubans have immigrated, many to the United States.
